name: Scheduled tasks
description:
1. You asked for recurring tasks: attach a schedule to a task — e.g. "every friday at noon review the week and create a report" — with each run either seeing the previous history or starting clean.
2. Backend v1 shipped: `autonomy/recurrence.py` parses rules (`every friday at noon`, `every 2 hours`, timezone), new task fields `schedule` / `schedule_context` / `schedule_column`, and a re-arm hook in `ActorService._consume_agenda` (history reopens the same card, clean forks a new one and links the closed one).
3. Entry points: `POST /api/chats/schedule`, a `context` parameter on `schedule_task`, and `schedule` / `schedule_context` accepted by `project_manager` create/update_task.
4. Tests: `test_recurrence.py` (18) + `test_recurrence_rearm.py` (11) → 29 passed, 0 failed; one red test was a test bug (compared against an already-mutated description), fixed without weakening it.
5. Client UI added (`chats.js` → `scheduleChat`, Repeat block in `TaskSettings.vue`), but not build-verified (`node` unavailable in the containers); full `qa_review_changes` ran 245 passed / 6 failed, all in files unrelated to this work.

**Good enough?** ok / next / what is wrong — `ok` ships it, `next` takes the first next task, `what is wrong` fixes this one.

messages.content:
This task involves tasks and calendar. I want to setup repetitive tasks in the calendar or, from a task, add a scheduler.

Example every friday noon review the week changes and create a report.
So I ust be able to add schedule to a task and codx-junior will execute it every friday.

We'll need to define if each execution can see history or start clean.

Implement the fist version, let me know when is ready to test

Now I have the full picture. One last read to patch the tool exactly:Now writing the first version. Core module first:Two facts confirmed before I close the increment: `_consume_agenda` is the single place where a wake is *consumed* (the re-arm hook), and `Chat` is a plain pydantic model where the new fields already landed. My previous patch added the `_rearm` **call** only — I'm adding the method now, plus the tests.Now the two entry points that let the user actually create a schedule — an HTTP route and the `schedule_task` tool:My last tool patch contained identity replacements (a slip) — the import landed but the logic did not. Fixing that properly now:Backend v1 is in and green. One increment, no UI yet.

**Confirmed:** `_consume_agenda` was the only place a wake is consumed, so a recurrence only needed a re-arm hook there; `Chat` is a plain pydantic model, so the new fields are persisted by the existing `update_chat_metadata`. **Ruled out:** nothing in the worker loop needed to change — the alarm clock is per task, not per actor.

## What happened

You asked for recurring tasks: "every friday at noon review the week and create a report", attachable to a task, with a choice between seeing history or starting clean.

## What I did

- **New** `api/codx/junior/autonomy/recurrence.py` — parses `every friday at noon`, `every day at 09:00`, `every weekday at 09:00`, `every 2 hours`, optional `@Europe/Madrid`; returns the next instant (never in the past) and the canonical text.
- `api/codx/junior/db.py` — task fields `schedule`, `schedule_context` (`history`|`clean`), `schedule_column`.
- `api/codx/junior/autonomy/service.py` — after a shift delivers a **closed** task that has a `schedule`: `history` reopens the same card (status todo, progress 0, back to its home column) and arms the next occurrence; `clean` creates a brand-new card with the same name/description/board/profiles but no messages and no parent, and closes the old one with a link.
- `api/codx/junior/api/chat.py` — `POST /chats/schedule` (`chat_id`, `schedule`, `context`, `timezone`); empty `schedule` clears the series.
- `api/codx/junior/tools/schedule_task_tool.py` — `when` now also accepts a recurrence plus `context`.
- `api/tests/test_recurrence.py` — 18 tests: **18 passed, 0 failed** (`pytest:api`).

## Demo

```
curl -X POST <API_BASE>/chats/schedule -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"chat_id":"<TASK_ID>","schedule":"every friday at noon","context":"history","timezone":"Europe/Madrid"}'
```
→ returns `{"schedule":"every friday at 12:00 @Europe/Madrid","wake_at":"<next friday 12:00 local>", "next_run": ...}`. The autonomy worker must be enabled and an actor must own that board for the run to happen.

## Next tasks

- `quick` — Task card UI: a "Repeat" control (recurrence + history/clean) calling `/chats/schedule`, showing the next run.
- `quick` — declare `context` as a real `schedule_task` parameter (today it arrives via `kwargs`) and teach `project_manager` create/update to accept `schedule`.
- `max` — cover the re-arm itself with tests (history vs clean card, column reset, worker never spins) + full suite, then the calendar view.

**Good enough?** ok / next / what is wrong — `ok` ships it, `next` takes the first next task, `what is wrong` fixes this one.

```python
"""
Recurring task schedules.

A task may carry a *recurrence* (``Chat.schedule``) instead of a one-shot
``wake_at``: codx-junior then re-arms the alarm clock every time the task has
been delivered to an autonomous actor, so "every friday at noon review the week
and write the report" keeps running without a human.

The recurrence is kept as **canonical text** (``"every friday at 12:00
@Europe/Madrid"``) so it stays readable in the task card and in the database,
and it is parsed on demand by :func:`parse_schedule` /
:func:`next_occurrence`.

Supported forms (v1, case insensitive):

* ``every day at 12:00``, ``daily 09:00``, ``every day at noon``
* ``every friday at 12:00``, ``every fri noon``, ``weekly on monday 09:00``
* ``every weekday at 09:00``, ``every mon,thu 18:00``
* ``every 2 hours``, ``every 30m``, ``every 1 hour``
* an optional trailing ``@Europe/Madrid`` (or `` in Europe/Madrid``) sets the
  zone the clock time is interpreted in (default UTC).

The module is dependency-free (``zoneinfo`` from the stdlib) so it can be
imported from the tool layer, the API and the autonomy worker alike.
"""
```

```python
"""
Recurring task schedules.

``Chat.wake_at`` is a one-shot alarm clock: the autonomy worker delivers the
task once and the wake is consumed. A *recurrence* turns it into a series: the
task also carries ``Chat.schedule`` (canonical text such as
``"every friday at 12:00 @Europe/Madrid"``) and the runtime re-arms ``wake_at``
to the next occurrence every time a shift delivered the task, so "every friday
at noon review the week and write the report" keeps running without a human.

Why canonical text instead of a cron object: the value is stored in the task
card (JSON), it must stay readable for the human reviewing the board, and it
must survive being written by a model through a tool. Parsing is cheap and
deterministic, so the rule is parsed on demand.

Supported forms (v1, case insensitive, optional trailing ``@Zone`` / `` in
Zone`` for the zone the clock time is interpreted in, UTC by default):

* ``every day at 12:00``, ``daily 09:00``, ``every day at noon``
* ``every friday at 12:00``, ``every fri noon``, ``weekly on monday 09:00``
* ``every weekday at 09:00``, ``every mon,thu 18:00``, ``every weekend 10:00``
* ``every 2 hours``, ``every 30m``, ``every 1h``

A day/week recurrence without a clock time defaults to 09:00
(:data:`DEFAULT_HOUR`).

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""
```

```python
def parse_schedule(value, timezone_name: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[Schedule]:
    text = str(value or "").strip()
    if not text:
        return None
    zone_name = (timezone_name or "").strip() or "UTC"
    zone_match = _ZONE_RE.search(text)
    if zone_match:
        zone_name = zone_match.group(1)
        text = text[: zone_match.start()].strip()
    lowered = text.lower().strip().rstrip(".")
    if not _PREFIX_RE.match(lowered):
        return None
    body = _PREFIX_RE.sub("", lowered, count=1).strip()
    if not body:
        return None

    interval = _INTERVAL_RE.match(body)
    if interval:
        seconds = _interval_seconds(interval.group(1), interval.group(2))
        if not seconds:
            return None
        return Schedule(kind="interval", timezone_name=zone_name, interval_seconds=seconds)

    hour, minute, body = _extract_clock(body)
    weekdays = _extract_weekdays(body)
    rest = _WORD_RE.findall(body)
    daily_words = {"day", "daily", "days"}
    if weekdays:
        kind = "weekly"
    elif any(word in daily_words for word in rest):
        kind = "daily"
        weekdays = ()
    else:
        return None
    return Schedule(kind=kind, timezone_name=zone_name, hour=hour, minute=minute, weekdays=tuple(weekdays))
```

```python
def _extract_clock(body: str) -> Tuple[int, int, str]:
    for word, (hour, minute) in CLOCK_WORDS.items():
        match = re.search(rf"\b{word}\b", body, re.I)
        if match:
            return hour, minute, (body[:match.start()] + " " + body[match.end():]).strip()
    match = _AT_CLOCK_RE.search(body)
    if match:
        hour = int(match.group(1))
        minute = int(match.group(2) or 0)
        meridiem = (match.group(3) or "").lower()
        if meridiem == "pm" and hour < 12: hour += 12
        if meridiem == "am" and hour == 12: hour = 0
        if not (0 <= hour <= 23 and 0 <= minute <= 59):
            return DEFAULT_HOUR, 0, body
        return hour, minute, (body[:match.start()] + " " + body[match.end():]).strip()
```

```python
def _extract_weekdays(body: str) -> List[int]:
    found: List[int] = []
    for word in _WORD_RE.findall(body):
        if word in ("weekday", "weekdays"):
            candidates = list(_WEEKDAY)
        elif word in ("weekend", "weekends"):
            candidates = list(_WEEKEND)
        elif word in WEEKDAYS:
            candidates = [WEEKDAYS[word]]
        else:
            continue
        for day in candidates:
            if day not in found:
                found.append(day)
    return sorted(found)
```

```python
@router.post("/chats/schedule")
async def api_schedule_chat(request: Request):
    """
    Add, change or clear the recurrence of a task.

    Expected JSON payload:
        {
            "chat_id": "<chat UUID>",
            "schedule": "every friday at 12:00",   # empty clears it
            "context": "history" | "clean",        # how each run starts
            "timezone": "Europe/Madrid"            # clock zone (UTC default)
        }

    Returns the stored ``schedule``, the ``context`` and the ``wake_at`` the
    task was armed to (the next occurrence). Empty ``schedule`` makes the task
    one-shot again (its ``wake_at`` is kept if still in the future, cleared
    otherwise).
    """
    try:
        data = await request.json()
        codx_junior_session = request.state.codx_junior_session
        chat_manager = await run_in_threadpool(codx_junior_session.get_chat_manager)

        chat_id = (data or {}).get("chat_id")
        if not chat_id:
            return {"error": "missing chat_id"}
        chat = chat_manager.find_by_id(chat_id=chat_id)
        if not chat:
            return {"error": f"chat '{chat_id}' not found"}

        text = str(data.get("schedule") or "").strip()
        timezone_name = str(data.get("timezone") or "").strip() or None
        context = parse_schedule_context(data.get("context"))
        metadata: Dict[str, Any] = {"schedule_context": context}
        if not text:
            metadata["schedule"] = None
            metadata["schedule_column"] = None
            if is_due(getattr(chat, "wake_at", "")):
                metadata["wake_at"] = ""
            updated = chat_manager.update_chat_metadata(chat=chat, metadata=metadata)
            return {**_conversation_response(updated), "schedule": None, "context": context, "wake_at": getattr(updated, "wake_at", None)}

        rule = parse_schedule(text, timezone_name=timezone_name)
        if rule is None:
            return {"error": f"cannot understand schedule '{text}'. Try 'every friday at 12:00', 'every day at 09:00', 'every 2 hours' or 'every weekday at 09:00'"}
        wake_at = next_occurrence(rule)
        metadata.update({
            "schedule": rule.text(),
            "schedule_column": getattr(chat, "column", None),
            "wake_at": wake_at,
        })
        updated = chat_manager.update_chat_metadata(chat=chat, metadata=metadata)
        return {**_conversation_response(updated), "schedule": metadata["schedule"], "context": context, "wake_at": wake_at, "next_run": wake_at}
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.error("api_schedule_chat: unexpected error: %s", ex)
        return {"error": f"Failed to schedule chat: {str(ex)}"}
```

```python
    def _rearm(self, chat: Any, schedule: str) -> None:
        """
        Arm the next run of a recurring task after a shift delivered it.

        The task is always rescheduled to the next occurrence of its recurrence
        (never to an instant in the past, which would make the worker spin) and
        prepared according to ``schedule_context``:

        * ``history`` (default): the same task is reopened (status back to do,
          progress 0, column reset to ``schedule_column``), so the next run sees
          what the previous ones did.
        * ``clean``: a new card is created for the next run with the same name,
          description, board, profiles, files and tags but no messages and no
          parent; the finished card keeps its history and stops recurring.

        Args:
            chat: The closed task the shift just delivered.
            schedule: Its recurrence text.
        """
        chat_id = str(getattr(chat, "id", "") or "")
        rule = parse_schedule(schedule)
        manager = self._manager()
        if rule is None:
            logger.warning(
                "actors: task '%s' has an unreadable schedule '%s': wake consumed",
                chat_id, schedule,
            )
            try:
                chat.wake_at = ""
                manager.save_chat(chat=chat)
            except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                logger.warning("actors: cannot clear wake of '%s': %s", chat_id, ex)
            return

        wake_at = next_occurrence(rule)
        context = parse_context(getattr(chat, "schedule_context", None))
        home_column = (
            str(getattr(chat, "schedule_column", "") or "").strip()
            or str(getattr(chat, "column", "") or "").strip()
            or DEFAULT_COLUMN
        )
        try:
            if context != CONTEXT_CLEAN:
                chat.wake_at = wake_at
                chat.status = "todo"
                chat.progress = 0
                chat.column = home_column
                manager.save_chat(chat=chat)
                logger.info(
                    "actors: recurring task '%s' armed for %s (%s)",
                    chat_id, wake_at, rule.text(),
                )
                return

            from codx.junior.db import Chat as ChatModel, Message

            clone = ChatModel(
                name=getattr(chat, "name", "") or "",
                description=getattr(chat, "description", "") or "",
                board=getattr(chat, "board", "") or DEFAULT_BOARD,
                column=home_column,
                status="todo",
                priority=getattr(chat, "priority", None),
                wake_at=wake_at,
                progress=0,
                schedule=rule.text(),
                schedule_context=CONTEXT_CLEAN,
                schedule_column=home_column,
                profiles=list(getattr(chat, "profiles", []) or []),
                file_list=list(getattr(chat, "file_list", []) or []),
                tags=list(getattr(chat, "tags", []) or []),
                sprints=list(getattr(chat, "sprints", []) or []),
                project_id=getattr(chat, "project_id", None),
                owner_project_id=getattr(chat, "owner_project_id", None),
            )
            clone.messages.append(
                Message(
                    role="user",
                    content=(clone.description or clone.name or "").strip(),
                    profiles=clone.profiles,
                    files=clone.file_list,
                )
            )
            created = manager.save_chat(chat=clone)
            chat.schedule = None
            chat.wake_at = ""
            chat.description = (
                f"{getattr(chat, 'description', '') or ''}\n\n**Recurring:** the "
                f"next run is task `{getattr(created, 'id', '')}`"
            )[:8000]
            manager.save_chat(chat=chat)
            logger.info(
                "actors: recurring task '%s' (%s) continued as '%s'",
                chat_id, rule.text(), getattr(created, "id", ""),
            )
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            logger.warning("actors: cannot re-arm recurring task '%s': %s", chat_id, ex)
```

```python
@router.post("/chats/schedule")
async def api_schedule_chat(request: Request):
    """
    Add, change or clear the recurrence of a task.

    Expected JSON payload:
        {
            "chat_id": "<chat UUID>",
            "schedule": "every friday at 12:00",   # empty clears it
            "context": "history" | "clean",        # how each run starts
            "timezone": "Europe/Madrid"            # zone of the clock time
        }

    ``schedule`` accepts the recurrence forms understood by
    :mod:`codx.junior.autonomy.recurrence` ("every day at 09:00", "every friday
    at noon", "every weekday at 09:00", "every 2 hours"). The task is armed to
    the next occurrence and the autonomy runtime re-arms it after every run.

    Returns:
        The stored ``schedule``, its ``context`` and the ``wake_at``/``next_run``
        instant, or ``{"error": ...}``.
    """
    from codx.junior.autonomy.models import is_due
    from codx.junior.autonomy.recurrence import (
        next_occurrence,
        parse_context,
        parse_schedule,
    )

    try:
        data = await request.json()
        codx_junior_session = request.state.codx_junior_session
        chat_manager = await run_in_threadpool(codx_junior_session.get_chat_manager)

        chat_id = (data or {}).get("chat_id")
        if not chat_id:
            return {"error": "missing chat_id"}
        chat = chat_manager.find_by_id(chat_id=chat_id)
        if not chat:
            return {"error": f"chat '{chat_id}' not found"}

        text = str((data or {}).get("schedule") or "").strip()
        context = parse_context((data or {}).get("context"))
        timezone_name = str((data or {}).get("timezone") or "").strip() or None

        if not text:
            metadata = {"schedule": None, "schedule_column": None,
                        "schedule_context": context}
            if is_due(getattr(chat, "wake_at", "")):
                metadata["wake_at"] = ""
            updated = chat_manager.update_chat_metadata(chat=chat, metadata=metadata)
            return {...}

        rule = parse_schedule(text, timezone_name=timezone_name)
        if rule is None:
            return {
                "error": (
                    f"cannot understand schedule '{text}'. Try 'every friday at "
                    "12:00', 'every day at 09:00', 'every weekday at 09:00' or "
                    "'every 2 hours'"
                )
            }
        wake_at = next_occurrence(rule)
        updated = chat_manager.update_chat_metadata(
            chat=chat,
            metadata={
                "schedule": rule.text(),
                "schedule_context": context,
                "schedule_column": getattr(chat, "column", None),
                "wake_at": wake_at,
            },
        )
        return {
            "chat_id": getattr(updated, "id", chat_id),
            "name": getattr(updated, "name", None),
            "board": getattr(updated, "board", None),
            "column": getattr(updated, "column", None),
            "schedule": getattr(updated, "schedule", None),
            "context": getattr(updated, "schedule_context", None),
            "wake_at": getattr(updated, "wake_at", None),
            "next_run": wake_at,
        }
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.error("api_schedule_chat: unexpected error: %s", ex)
        return {"error": f"Failed to schedule chat: {str(ex)}"}
```

"""
Recurring task schedules.

``Chat.wake_at`` is a one-shot alarm clock: the autonomy worker delivers the
task once and the wake is consumed. A **recurrence** turns it into a series: the
task also carries ``Chat.schedule`` (canonical text such as
``"every friday at 12:00 @Europe/Madrid"``) and the runtime re-arms ``wake_at``
to the next occurrence every time a shift delivered the task. That is what makes
"every friday at noon review the week and write the report" keep running without
a human in the loop.

Why canonical *text* instead of a cron object: the rule is stored in the task
card (JSON), it must stay readable for the human reviewing the board, and it is
usually written by a model through a tool. Parsing is cheap and deterministic, so
the rule is parsed on demand instead of being kept as a second source of truth.

Supported forms (v1, case insensitive; an optional trailing ``@Zone`` or
`` in Zone`` sets the zone the clock time is interpreted in, UTC by default):

* ``every day at 12:00``, ``daily 09:00``, ``every day at noon``
* ``every friday at 12:00``, ``every fri noon``, ``weekly on monday 09:00``
* ``every weekday at 09:00``, ``every mon,thu 18:00``, ``every weekend 10:00``
* ``every 2 hours``, ``every 30m``, ``every 1h``

A day/week rule without a clock time defaults to :data:`DEFAULT_HOUR` (09:00).

The module only depends on the standard library so it can be imported from the
tool layer, the HTTP API and the autonomy worker alike.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, time as dt_time, timedelta, timezone as dt_timezone
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

UTC = dt_timezone.utc

#: Clock used when the rule names a day but no hour ("every friday").
DEFAULT_HOUR = 9

#: ``history`` keeps the task (and its conversation) between runs, so every run
#: sees what the previous ones did; ``clean`` starts every run in a brand new
#: card with no previous messages.

    zone_match = _ZONE_RE.search(text)

        zone_name = zone_match.group(1)

    lowered = text.lower().strip().rstrip(".")
    if not _PREFIX_RE.match(lowered):
        return None
    body = _PREFIX_RE.sub("", lowered, count=1).strip()

        seconds = _interval_seconds(interval.group(1), interval.group(2))
        if not seconds:

    elif tokens & {"day", "daily", "days"}:

        kind=kind,
        timezone_name=zone_name,
        hour=hour,
        minute=minute,
        weekdays=tuple(weekdays),

    """

    Args:
        schedule: The parsed rule.
        now: Reference instant (default: now, UTC).

    Returns:
        ISO-8601 UTC instant.
    """
    moment = now or datetime.now(tz=UTC)
    if moment.tzinfo is None:
        moment = moment.replace(tzinfo=UTC)

    if schedule.kind == "interval":
        period = max(60, int(schedule.interval_seconds or 0))
        return (moment + timedelta(seconds=period)).astimezone(UTC).isoformat()

    zone = schedule.zone()
    local = moment.astimezone(zone)
    weekdays = schedule.weekdays if schedule.kind == "weekly" else ()
    for offset in range(0, 8):
        day = (local + timedelta(days=offset)).date()

            continue
        candidate = datetime.combine(
            day, dt_time(schedule.hour, schedule.minute), tzinfo=zone

        if candidate > local:
            return candidate.astimezone(UTC).isoformat()

```py api/codx/junior/db.py
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unsent drafts (message composer state)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The text a user is still typing is persisted with the chat as ONE draft
# message (``Message.unsent == True``). It survives reloads and crashes, but it
# is NOT part of the conversation: it must never be listed, summarized, sent to
# the model, broadcast as a chat message, exported or counted by analytics.
# Persistence is delegated to the owner ``ChatManager`` (the only chat store);
# the imports are lazy because ``chat_manager`` imports this module.


def _visible_messages(messages: Optional[List[Message]]) -> List[Message]:
    """
    Return only the messages that belong to the conversation.

    Unsent drafts (``Message.unsent``) are filtered out here, so every reader
    that goes through this helper is draft-free by construction.

    :param messages: Message list of a chat (may be ``None``).
    :return: A new list without the unsent drafts.
    """
    return [message for message in (messages or []) if not message.unsent]


def conversation_response(chat: Any) -> Any:
    """
    Return a serialisation-ready COPY of *chat* without its unsent drafts.

    Every message endpoint answers with the WHOLE chat (``POST/PUT/DELETE
    /chats/message``, ``POST /chats/metadata``) and the client merges that
    payload message by message (``mergeMessages`` in ``store/chats.js``). A
    draft still held in memory would therefore come back as a conversation
    bubble: the same text appeared twice, once as the promoted draft and once
    as the real message.

    The chat is copied on purpose: stripping the draft MUST NOT mutate the
    object the caller still owns (the composer draft lives in the same store and
    a send that keeps the draft would otherwise destroy it as a side effect of
    building the response).

    :param chat: The chat returned by a message endpoint (``None`` and error
        payloads are returned untouched).
    :return: A copy of the chat with its ``unsent`` messages removed.
    """
    if chat is None or isinstance(chat, dict):
        return chat
    if not getattr(chat, "messages", None):
        return chat
    visible = _visible_messages(chat.messages)
    # Pydantic models (``Chat``) support a cheap model_copy; the fallback keeps
    # plain objects (tests, stubs) working without mutating them.
    try:
        return chat.model_copy(update={"messages": visible})
    except AttributeError:
        from copy import copy

        clone = copy(chat)
        clone.messages = visible
        return clone


def _find_unsent_message(chat: "Chat") -> Optional[Message]:
    """
    Return the unsent draft of *chat* (the most recent one when legacy data has
    more than one), or ``None`` when the chat has no draft.

    :param chat: Chat to inspect.
    :return: The draft message or ``None``.
    """
    for message in reversed(chat.messages or []):
        if message.unsent:
            return message
    return None


def _resolve_chat_manager(chat_id: str, chat_manager: Any = None) -> Any:
    """
    Resolve the ``ChatManager`` that stores *chat_id*.

    The manager is injectable (``chat_manager``) because the API layer already
    holds the session manager; otherwise the projects are searched the same way
    ``/api/chats/message`` resolves a chat id.

    :param chat_id: Chat whose store is needed.
    :param chat_manager: Optional already-resolved manager.
    :return: The manager holding the chat, or ``None`` when it is unknown.
    """
    if chat_manager is not None:
        return chat_manager

    from codx.junior.chat_manager import ChatManager
    from codx.junior.project.project_discover import find_all_projects

    try:
        projects = find_all_projects()
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        logger.warning("draft: cannot list projects for chat '%s': %s", chat_id, ex)
        return None

    for settings in projects.values():
        try:
            manager = ChatManager(settings=settings)
            if manager.find_by_id(chat_id) is not None:
                return manager
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            logger.warning(
                "draft: project scan failed for chat '%s': %s", chat_id, ex
            )
    return None


def get_unsent_message(chat_id: str, chat_manager: Any = None) -> Optional[Message]:
    """
    Return the unsent draft of *chat_id*.

    Only the client composer that owns the draft should call this: the returned
    message is not part of the conversation (see :func:`_visible_messages`).

    :param chat_id: Chat whose draft is requested.
    :param chat_manager: Optional already-resolved ``ChatManager``.
    :return: The draft message, or ``None`` when the chat has no draft.
    """
    if not chat_id:
        return None
    manager = _resolve_chat_manager(chat_id, chat_manager)
    chat = manager.find_by_id(chat_id) if manager else None
    if chat is None:
        return None
    return _find_unsent_message(chat)


def upsert_unsent_message(
    chat_id: str,
    content: str,
    author: Optional[str] = None,
    chat_manager: Any = None,
) -> Message:
    """
    Create or replace the single unsent draft of *chat_id*.

    The existing draft ``doc_id`` is reused when updating, so the client keeps
    a stable key while typing. The chat keeps at most ONE unsent message.

    :param chat_id: Chat owning the draft.
    :param content: Current composer text.
    :param author: Optional username of the composer (stored in ``Message.user``).
    :param chat_manager: Optional already-resolved ``ChatManager``.
    :return: The persisted draft message.
    :raises ValueError: When *chat_id* is missing or unknown.
    """
    if not chat_id:
        raise ValueError("upsert_unsent_message requires a chat_id")

    manager = _resolve_chat_manager(chat_id, chat_manager)
    chat = manager.find_by_id(chat_id) if manager else None
    if chat is None:
```

```py api/codx/junior/autonomy/service.py
"""
Application service of the actors.

One **shift** of one actor is a bounded pipeline:

    actor configuration -> boards -> agenda (due tasks)
        -> shift card on the desk board -> one or more agent turns with the
        whole tool set -> report on the card -> state store

This module is the **single runtime**. It used to be two:

* ``autonomy`` — a profile woke up, read its board and worked with every tool;
* ``board_manager`` — a profile reviewed a board and answered with a JSON
  action contract that was validated and applied afterwards.

The only real differences were the prompt (role), the tool policy and whether a
shift is one turn or turns until the work is done. Those are now three fields of
:class:`~codx.junior.autonomy.models.ActorConfig` (``role``, ``policy``,
``session``), and both entry points share this pipeline. The JSON contract is
gone: an actor uses the same task tools a human uses, so every change it makes
is visible on the board exactly like a human change.

Two things make this different from a chat:

* the actor is woken by the scheduler, not by a user, and it must decide by
  itself what to do (see :mod:`.prompts`);
* every follow-up becomes a **scheduled task** (``wake_at``), which is what makes
  "check that system again in two days" possible without a human in the loop.

The **weekly schedule** is enforced here as well: an actor only starts a shift
inside its availability window, and a due task that falls outside the window is
kept (its ``wake_at`` is not consumed) until the next opening.

Everything heavy (the AI stack, the chat engine) is imported lazily and both the
turn runner and the chat factory are injectable, so the whole pipeline can be
tested offline and the module can be imported by the API without the AI deps.

    def _event_manager(self) -> Any:

        request session, so ``event_manager`` used to be ``None`` and the first
        ``ChatEngine`` event raised ``AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no
        attribute 'chat_event'``. Every real turn failed before reaching the
        model. Build the same project-scoped manager the API middleware uses
        when none was injected.
        """

        a guarantee: a linked ``codx-junior`` profile still handed the model the
        shell, git and file tools. The allowlist is applied by ``ChatEngine``
        after it collects the profile tools, so the restriction is structural.

        granted to its profile (``mcp_*``). That is what lets a support agent
        work the board and call the CRM/helpdesk without ever receiving the
        shell or repository tools.
        """
        if config.policy != C.POLICY_BOARD:
            return None
        allowed = set(C.BOARD_ONLY_TOOLS)
        for tool in getattr(profile, "tools", None) or []:
            name = str(tool or "").strip()
            if name.startswith("mcp_"):

    def actors(

            A profile that cannot be read is skipped (the catalogue is never a
            single point of failure).
        """
        actors: Dict[str, Tuple[Any, ActorConfig]] = {}

            profiles = self._profiles().list_all_profiles() or []
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            logger.exception("actors: cannot list profiles: %s", ex)

    def collect_tasks(

    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Return the snapshot of the watched boards handed to the actor."""
        moment = now or utcnow()
        watched = {str(board or "").strip() for board in boards or [] if str(board or "").strip()}
        if not watched:
            return []
        snapshot: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for chat in self._manager().list_chats() or []:
            board = str(getattr(chat, "board", "") or "").strip()
            if board not in watched:
                continue
            if getattr(chat, "is_template", False):
                continue
            if str(getattr(chat, "mode", "") or "").strip().lower() == "channel":
                continue
            closed = self._is_closed(chat)
            if closed and not config.include_done:
                continue
            snapshot.append({
                "id": str(getattr(chat, "id", "") or ""),
                "name": _clip(getattr(chat, "name", ""), 300),
                "description": _clip(getattr(chat, "description", ""), MAX_DESCRIPTION_CHARS),
                "last_message": self._last_message(chat),
                "board": board,
                "column": str(getattr(chat, "column", "") or ""),
                "status": str(getattr(chat, "status", "") or ""),
                "wake_at": str(getattr(chat, "wake_at", "") or ""),
                "priority": str(getattr(chat, "priority", "") or ""),
                "due_date": str(getattr(chat, "due_date", "") or ""),
                "assignees": list(getattr(chat, "assignees", []) or []),
                "profiles": list(getattr(chat, "profiles", []) or []),
                "tags": list(getattr(chat, "tags", []) or []),
                "progress": int(getattr(chat, "progress", 0) or 0),
                "created_at": str(getattr(chat, "created_at", "") or ""),
                "updated_at": str(getattr(chat, "updated_at", "") or ""),
                "done": closed,
                "due_now": is_due(getattr(chat, "wake_at", ""), moment),
            })

        # Due and open tasks first, then the most recently touched ones: when the
        # boards have more cards than the prompt budget, the shift must see the
        # work that needs it now.
        snapshot.sort(key=lambda task: task.get("updated_at") or "", reverse=True)
        snapshot.sort(key=lambda task: 0 if task.get("due_now") else 1)
        snapshot.sort(key=lambda task: 1 if task.get("done") else 0)
        limit = max(1, min(int(config.max_tasks or C.DEFAULT_MAX_TASKS), C.MAX_TASKS_LIMIT))
        return snapshot[:limit]

    def due_agenda(
        self,
        boards: List[str],
        config: ActorConfig,
        now: Optional[datetime] = None,
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Return the tasks whose ``wake_at`` is due (open ones only)."""
        moment = now or utcnow()
        items = [
            task
            for task in self.collect_tasks(boards, config, now=moment)
            if task.get("due_now") and not task.get("done")
        ]
        items.sort(key=lambda task: task.get("wake_at") or "")
        return items[: max(1, config.max_agenda)]

    @staticmethod
    def _is_closed(chat: Any) -> bool:
        """Return True when the task is finished and must never wake again."""
        status = str(getattr(chat, "status", "") or "").strip().lower()
        if status in C.CLOSED_STATUSES:
            return True
        column = str(getattr(chat, "column", "") or "").strip().lower()
        if column in C.CLOSED_STATUSES:
            return True
        return bool(getattr(chat, "done", False))

    @staticmethod
    def _last_message(chat: Any) -> str:
        """Return the last visible message content of *chat*."""
        for message in reversed(getattr(chat, "messages", []) or []):
            if getattr(message, "hide", False):
                continue
            content = _clip(getattr(message, "content", ""), MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS)
            if content:
                return content
        return ""

    # -- schedule ---------------------------------------------------------

    def is_within_schedule(
        self, config: ActorConfig, now: Optional[datetime] = None
    ) -> bool:
        """Return True when the weekly availability of the actor is open."""
        if not self._schedule_enforced():
            return True
        return config.schedule.normalized().is_open(now or utcnow())

    def next_opening(
        self, config: ActorConfig, now: Optional[datetime] = None
    ) -> Optional[datetime]:
        """Return the next instant the actor may work (None when paused)."""
        moment = now or utcnow()
        if not self._schedule_enforced():
            return moment
        return config.schedule.normalized().next_opening(moment)

    @staticmethod
    def _schedule_enforced() -> bool:
        """Return True when the availability windows must be respected."""
        from .worker import schedule_enforced

        return schedule_enforced()

    def budget_cap(
        self,
        config: ActorConfig,
        daily_spent: float,
    ) -> Optional[float]:
        """
        Return the effective cap of one shift, or ``None`` when uncapped.

        The daily budget is a *hard* limit: when less than the shift budget is
        left today, the remaining day amount becomes the cap. ``0`` means "no
        cap" for either budget, matching the configuration semantics.
        """
        caps: List[float] = []
        if config.budget_cxjcoins > 0:
            caps.append(float(config.budget_cxjcoins))
        if config.daily_budget_cxjcoins > 0:
            caps.append(
                max(0.0, float(config.daily_budget_cxjcoins) - max(0.0, float(daily_spent or 0.0)))
            )
        return min(caps) if caps else None

    def next_daily_wake(
        self,
        config: ActorConfig,
        now: Optional[datetime] = None,
    ) -> str:
        """
        Return the first shift instant after the UTC daily ledger resets.

        When the daily budget is exhausted the actor must not retry on its
        normal cadence: it would be skipped every few minutes and keep rewriting
        state. The next eligible instant is the next UTC midnight (adjusted by
        the availability window when one is configured).
        """
        moment = now or utcnow()
        tomorrow = (moment.astimezone(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=1)).date()
        candidate = datetime(
            tomorrow.year, tomorrow.month, tomorrow.day, tzinfo=timezone.utc
        )
        opening = self.next_opening(config, candidate)
        return opening.isoformat() if opening is not None else ""

    def next_wake_at(
        self,
        config: ActorConfig,
        state: ActorState,
        now: Optional[datetime] = None,
    ) -> str:
        """
        Return the next planned wake of the actor (empty when disabled).

        The cadence is measured from the **finish** of the previous shift, not
        its start: a shift that runs longer than ``interval_minutes`` used to be
        due again immediately, producing back-to-back shifts. The value also
        accounts for the weekly schedule: an actor that is outside its window
        reports the next opening instead of the cadence.
        """
        if not config.enabled or state.running:
            return ""
        moment = now or utcnow()
        if (
            config.daily_budget_cxjcoins > 0
            and state.day_spent(moment.date().isoformat()) >= config.daily_budget_cxjcoins
        ):
            return self.next_daily_wake(config, moment)
        planned = parse_iso(state.wake_at)
        if planned is None:
            last = parse_iso(state.last_finished_at) or parse_iso(state.last_shift_at)
            if last is None:
                # First wake only: an actor declaration may carry an initial
                # instant. Once the actor has shifted, the runtime state owns
                # the schedule.
                planned = parse_iso(config.wake_at) or moment
            else:
                planned = last + timedelta(minutes=config.interval_minutes)
        if planned < moment:
            planned = moment
        opening = self.next_opening(config, planned)
        return opening.isoformat() if opening is not None else ""

    def is_due(
        self,
        config: ActorConfig,
        state: ActorState,
        now: Optional[datetime] = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Return True when the actor should take a shift now.

        A manual wake (``state.wake_requested``) is always honoured: it is an
        explicit human decision. Automatic wakes only happen inside the weekly
        availability window, which is the whole point of quiet hours.
        """
        if not config.enabled:
            return False
        moment = now or utcnow()
        if (
            config.daily_budget_cxjcoins > 0
            and state.day_spent(moment.date().isoformat()) >= config.daily_budget_cxjcoins
        ):
            # A hard budget is not bypassed by a manual wake: the shift would be
            # rejected by _execute anyway, so report it as not due and let the
            # next UTC day (or the next schedule opening) pick it up.
            return False
        if state.wake_requested:
            # A manual wake with a future ``when`` is a scheduled manual wake:
            # honour the instant instead of running immediately. Without a
            # wake instant it means "now".
            requested = parse_iso(state.wake_at)
            if requested is None or requested <= moment:
                return True
            return False
        # A shift can run for minutes; a "running" state is only abandoned when
        # it is far older than the runtime limit.
        if state.running:
            started = parse_iso(state.last_shift_at)
            if started is not None:
                age = (moment - started).total_seconds()
                limit = max(C.STALE_SHIFT_SECONDS, config.max_runtime_minutes * 60 + 300)
                if age < limit:
                    return False
        if not self.is_within_schedule(config, moment):
            return False
        planned = parse_iso(state.wake_at)
        if planned is None and not state.last_shift_at:
            # First wake only, from the declaration.
            planned = parse_iso(config.wake_at)
        if planned is not None:
            return planned <= moment
        last = parse_iso(state.last_finished_at) or parse_iso(state.last_shift_at)
        if last is None:
            return True
        return moment >= last + timedelta(minutes=config.interval_minutes)

    # -- status -----------------------------------------------------------

    def status(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the configuration + runtime state of every actor."""
        stored = self.store.load().get("agents") or {}
        entries: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for name, (profile, config) in self.actors(include_disabled=True).items():
            try:
                state = ActorState(**(stored.get(name) or {}))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                state = ActorState(actor=name)
            entries.append(self._entry(name, profile, config, state))
        return {
            "actors": entries,
            # Legacy key: the UI reads `agents`.
            "agents": entries,
            "worker_present": self.store.worker_present()
            or any(entry["state"].get("running") for entry in entries),
            "defaults": {
                "role": C.DEFAULT_ROLE,
                "policy": C.DEFAULT_POLICY,
                "session": C.DEFAULT_SESSION,
                "mode": C.DEFAULT_MODE,
                "interval_minutes": C.DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MINUTES,
                "max_agenda": C.DEFAULT_MAX_AGENDA,
                "max_turns": C.DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS,
                "max_runtime_minutes": C.DEFAULT_MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES,
                "columns": list(C.DEFAULT_COLUMNS),
                "weekdays": list(C.WEEKDAYS),
                "timezone": C.DEFAULT_TIMEZONE,
            },
        }

            },
            "due": self.is_due(config, state),
            "next_wake_at": self.next_wake_at(config, state),
            "daily_spent": state.day_spent(),
            "worker_present": self.store.worker_present(),
        }

    def request_wake(self, actor: str, when: str = "") -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Record "take a shift now" (or at *when*) for *actor*.

        The API never runs a shift inline: it writes the intent and the
        background worker executes it, exactly like the orchestration runtime.
        """
        from .models import parse_when

        name, _profile, config = self.resolve_actor(actor)
        wake_at = parse_when(when) if when else ""
        state = self.store.request_wake(name, board=config.desk_board, wake_at=wake_at)
        self._emit(name, "wake", "Shift requested", board=config.desk_board)
        return {
            "queued": True,
            "actor": name,
            "board": config.desk_board,
            "wake_at": wake_at,
            "state": state.public(),
        }

    def schedule_wake(self, actor: str, when: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Set the next planned wake of *actor* (the actor schedules itself)."""
        from .models import parse_when

        name, _profile, config = self.resolve_actor(actor)
        wake_at = parse_when(when)
        if not wake_at:
            raise ValueError(f"cannot understand the schedule '{when}'")
        state = self.store.set_wake_at(name, wake_at)
        self._emit(name, "scheduled", f"Next shift scheduled at {wake_at}",
                   board=config.desk_board)
        return {
            "actor": name,
            "board": config.desk_board,
            "wake_at": wake_at,
            "state": state.public(),
        }

    # -- shifts -----------------------------------------------------------

    async def run_due(self, force: bool = False) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Take a shift with every actor that is due (or every actor when forced)."""
        results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for name, (_profile, config) in self.actors().items():
            state = self.store.get_state(name)
            if not force and not self.is_due(config, state):
                continue
            results.append(await self.run_shift(name, force=True))
        return results

    async def run_shift(
        self,
        actor: str,
        *,
        force: bool = False,
        trigger: str = "schedule",
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Run one shift of *actor*.

        Args:
            actor: Profile name of the actor.
            force: Run even when the schedule says it is not due.
            trigger: What caused the shift (``schedule``, ``wake``, ``api``).

        Returns:
            The public payload of the actor (config, state, boards, schedule).
        """
        try:
            name, profile, config = self.resolve_actor(actor)
        except ValueError as ex:
            return {"actor": actor, "agent": actor, "error": str(ex)}

        if not force and not self.is_within_schedule(config):
            state = self.store.get_state(name)
            self._emit(
                name, "skipped",
                "Outside the availability window of the actor",
                board=config.desk_board,
            )
            payload = self._entry(name, profile, config, state)
            payload["skipped"] = C.STOP_SCHEDULE
            return payload

        with self.store.shift_lock(name) as acquired:
            if not acquired:
                return self._entry(name, profile, config, self.store.get_state(name))

            state = self.store.mutate_state(
                name, lambda current: self._started(current, name, config.desk_board)
            )
            self._emit(name, "started", "Shift started", board=config.desk_board)
            report = await self._execute(
                name=name, profile=profile, config=config, trigger=trigger, state=state
            )
            def _finalize(current: ActorState) -> ActorState:
                """Apply the report atomically (a Wake during the shift wins)."""
                # A user pressing Wake while the shift was running must not be
                # lost: mark_finished clears the flag, so capture it first.
                pending_wake = bool(current.wake_requested)
                pending_wake_at = str(current.wake_at or "")
                current.mark_finished(report)
                if report.stop_reason == C.STOP_DAILY_BUDGET:
                    # Hard budget wins over a pending manual wake; retry after
                    # the UTC day resets (or the next schedule opening).
                    current.wake_requested = False
                    daily_wake = self.next_daily_wake(config)
                    existing = parse_iso(current.wake_at)
                    proposed = parse_iso(daily_wake)
                    if proposed is not None and (
                        existing is None or existing < proposed
                    ):
                        current.wake_at = daily_wake
                elif pending_wake:
                    current.wake_requested = True
                    current.wake_at = pending_wake_at
                elif not current.wake_at:
                    current.wake_at = self.next_wake_at(config, current)
                return current

            state = self.store.mutate_state(name, _finalize)
            if config.notify:
                self._emit(name, "finished", report.report or report.error,
                           board=config.desk_board, status=report.status,
                           cost=report.cost_cxjcoins)
            logger.info(
                "actors: shift of '%s' finished status=%s stop=%s cost=%.6f turns=%d",
                name, report.status, report.stop_reason, report.cost_cxjcoins,
                report.turns,
            )
            return self._entry(name, profile, config, state)

    async def run_actor(
        self,
        *,
        actor: str,
        profile: Any,
        config: ActorConfig,
        trigger: str = "board",
        state: Optional[ActorState] = None,
    ) -> ShiftReport:
        """
        Run one shift of an actor declared outside the profile catalogue.

        This is the entry point the board manager uses: the configuration lives
        on the board, the execution is the very same pipeline. Nothing is
        persisted in the actor store — the caller owns that state.
        """
        config = config.normalized()
        return await self._execute(
            name=actor,
            profile=profile,
            config=config,
            trigger=trigger,
            state=state or ActorState(actor=actor),
        )

    async def _execute(
        self,
        *,
        name: str,
        profile: Any,
        config: ActorConfig,
        trigger: str,
        state: ActorState,
    ) -> ShiftReport:
        """
        Core shift pipeline shared by every actor source.

        Returns the :class:`ShiftReport`; the caller decides where to persist it.
        """
        boards = config.watched_boards
        desk = config.desk_board
        report = ShiftReport(actor=name, agent=name, board=desk, role=config.role)
        started = time.monotonic()
        total_cost = 0.0
        contents: List[str] = []
        agenda: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        shift_chat: Any = None
        stop_reason = ""
        dry_run = config.mode == C.MODE_DRY_RUN
        daily_spent = state.day_spent()

        # Hard daily gate: an exhausted day must not pay for even one turn.
        if config.daily_budget_cxjcoins > 0 and daily_spent >= config.daily_budget_cxjcoins:
            report.status = C.STATE_BUDGET
            report.stop_reason = C.STOP_DAILY_BUDGET
            report.error = (
                f"The daily budget is exhausted: {daily_spent:.4f} / "
                f"{config.daily_budget_cxjcoins:.4f} cxjcoins"
            )
            report.duration_seconds = time.monotonic() - started
            return report

        budget_cap = self.budget_cap(config, daily_spent)
        allowed_tools = self.tool_allowlist(config, profile)

        try:
            if not dry_run:
                self.ensure_boards(config)
                self._close_stale_shift_cards(
                    name, desk, config.max_runtime_minutes * 60 + 300
                )
            tasks = self.collect_tasks(boards, config)
            agenda = [
                task for task in tasks
                if task.get("due_now") and not task.get("done")
            ][: max(1, config.max_agenda)]
            report.agenda = [
                AgendaItem(chat_id=task["id"], name=task["name"],
                           wake_at=task.get("wake_at") or "")
                for task in agenda
            ]

            instructions = self._instructions(profile, config)
            system = prompts.build_shift_system(
                actor=name,
                board=desk,
                boards=boards,
                role=config.role,
                policy=config.policy,
                instructions=instructions,
                budget=config.budget_cxjcoins,
                daily_budget=config.daily_budget_cxjcoins,
                minutes=config.max_runtime_minutes,
                schedule=config.schedule.describe(),
                dry_run=dry_run,
            )
            prompt = prompts.build_shift_prompt(
                actor=name,
                board=desk,
                boards=boards,
                role=config.role,
                now=utcnow_iso(),
                trigger=trigger,
                shift_number=state.shifts,
                last_shift=state.last_summary,
                instructions=instructions,
                agenda=agenda,
                tasks=tasks,
            )

            max_turns = (
                config.max_turns
                if config.session == C.SESSION_UNTIL_DONE else 1
            )
            remaining = [
                task for task in self.collect_tasks(boards, config)
                if not task.get("done")
            ]

            while True:
                if report.turns >= max_turns:
                    stop_reason = (
                        C.STOP_TURNS if config.session == C.SESSION_UNTIL_DONE
                        else C.STOP_SINGLE
                    )
                    break
                elapsed = time.monotonic() - started
                if elapsed >= config.max_runtime_minutes * 60:
                    stop_reason = C.STOP_RUNTIME
                    break
                if config.budget_cxjcoins > 0 \
                        and total_cost >= config.budget_cxjcoins:
                    stop_reason = C.STOP_BUDGET
                    break
                if config.daily_budget_cxjcoins > 0 \
                        and (daily_spent + total_cost) >= config.daily_budget_cxjcoins:
                    stop_reason = C.STOP_DAILY_BUDGET
                    break

                timeout_seconds = max(
                    30,
                    int(config.max_runtime_minutes * 60 - elapsed),
                )
                if report.turns == 0:
                    turn_prompt = prompt
                else:
                    turn_prompt = prompts.build_continue_prompt(
                        turn=report.turns + 1,
                        max_turns=max_turns,
                        remaining=remaining,
                    )

                if dry_run:
                    content, cost, shift_chat = await self._dry_run(
                        name=name, board=desk, system=system, prompt=turn_prompt,
                        agenda=agenda, timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
                    )
                elif shift_chat is None:
                    content, cost, shift_chat = await self._active_turn(
                        name=name, board=desk, system=system, prompt=turn_prompt,
                        agenda=agenda, timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
                        tool_allowlist=allowed_tools, budget_cap=budget_cap,
                    )
                else:
                    content, cost = await self._continue_turn(
                        chat=shift_chat, system=system, prompt=turn_prompt,
                        timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
                        tool_allowlist=allowed_tools,
                    )

                report.turns += 1
                total_cost += max(0.0, float(cost or 0.0))
                if content:
                    contents.append(content)

                # A dry run is always one pass and writes nothing.
                if dry_run:
                    stop_reason = C.STOP_SINGLE
                    break
                # Budget exhaustion wins over the session shape: report it as
                # the stop reason even when the session would have ended here.
                if config.budget_cxjcoins > 0 \
                        and total_cost >= config.budget_cxjcoins:
                    stop_reason = C.STOP_BUDGET
                    break
                if config.daily_budget_cxjcoins > 0 \
                        and (daily_spent + total_cost) >= config.daily_budget_cxjcoins:
                    stop_reason = C.STOP_DAILY_BUDGET
                    break
                if config.session != C.SESSION_UNTIL_DONE:
                    stop_reason = C.STOP_SINGLE
                    break
                remaining = [
                    task for task in self.collect_tasks(boards, config)
                    if not task.get("done")
                ]
                if not remaining:
                    stop_reason = C.STOP_DONE
                    break

            content = "\n\n---\n\n".join(contents)
            report.shift_chat_id = str(getattr(shift_chat, "id", "") or "")
            report.summary = _clip(self._summary_from(content), 8000)
            report.report = _clip(content, 20000)
            report.cost_cxjcoins = total_cost
            report.stop_reason = stop_reason
            if stop_reason in (C.STOP_BUDGET, C.STOP_DAILY_BUDGET):
                report.status = C.STATE_BUDGET
            else:
                report.status = C.STATE_OK if contents else C.STATE_NO_WORK
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            report.status = C.STATE_ERROR
            report.stop_reason = C.STOP_RUNTIME
            report.error = (
                f"The shift exceeded {config.max_runtime_minutes} minutes and "
                "was cancelled"
            )
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            logger.exception("actors: shift of '%s' failed: %s", name, ex)
            report.status = C.STATE_ERROR
            report.error = str(ex)

        # Only a shift that actually ran and did not fail may settle its agenda.
        # A dry run never writes; an error must keep the due tasks for the next
        # attempt; tasks left due (not closed/rescheduled) stay due so the work
        # is retried instead of silently disappearing.
        if not dry_run and report.status != C.STATE_ERROR and report.turns > 0:
            self._consume_agenda(agenda)

        report.duration_seconds = time.monotonic() - started
        if shift_chat is not None:
            error = report.error if report.status == C.STATE_ERROR else ""
            self._close_shift_card(shift_chat, error=error)
        return report

    async def _active_turn(
        self,
        *,
        name: str,
        board: str,
        system: str,
        prompt: str,
        agenda: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        timeout_seconds: int,
        tool_allowlist: Optional[set] = None,
        budget_cap: Optional[float] = None,
    ) -> Tuple[str, float, Any]:
        """Create the shift card and run the first agent turn on it."""
        chat = self._create_shift_card(
            name=name, board=board, prompt=prompt, agenda=agenda,
            budget_cap=budget_cap,
        )
        try:
            runner = self._runner_for()
            await asyncio.wait_for(
                runner(chat=chat, system=system, tool_allowlist=tool_allowlist),
                timeout=timeout_seconds,
            )
        except BaseException as ex:
            # The card exists before the turn starts. If the turn is cancelled,
            # times out or raises, the caller never receives ``chat``, so this is
            # the only place that can move the card out of ``Working``.
            self._close_shift_card(chat, error=str(ex) or ex.__class__.__name__)
            raise
        content, cost = self._read_turn(chat)
        return content, cost, chat

    async def _continue_turn(
        self,
        *,
        chat: Any,
        system: str,
        prompt: str,
        timeout_seconds: int,
        tool_allowlist: Optional[set] = None,
    ) -> Tuple[str, float]:
        """Run another turn of the same shift on the same card."""
        cost_before = self._chat_cost(chat)
        self._manager().add_message(chat=chat, message=self._user_message(prompt))
        runner = self._runner_for()
        await asyncio.wait_for(
            runner(chat=chat, system=system, tool_allowlist=tool_allowlist),
            timeout=timeout_seconds,
        )
        content, _cost = self._read_turn(chat)
        return content, max(0.0, self._chat_cost(chat) - cost_before)

    async def _dry_run(
        self,
        *,
        name: str,
        board: str,
        system: str,
        prompt: str,
        agenda: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        timeout_seconds: int,
    ) -> Tuple[str, float, Any]:
        """
        Read-only shift: no tools, no card, no writes, just the report.

        A dry run is the honest way to preview an actor: the model is called
        directly (not through the agent loop, which is what exposes the tools)
        and no card is created or consumed. The caller gets ``None`` as the chat
        instead of a shift card.
        """
        from codx.junior.ai.ai import AI

        ai = AI(settings=self.settings, user=self.user, system=system)
        result = await asyncio.wait_for(
            ai.a_chat_run(prompt=prompt), timeout=timeout_seconds
        )
        content = str(getattr(result, "content", "") or "")
        cost = float(
            getattr(getattr(result, "cost", None), "iteration_cost_cxjcoins", 0) or 0
        )
        return content, cost, None

    async def _run_agent_turn(
        self,
        *,
        chat: Any,
        system: Optional[str] = None,
        tool_allowlist: Optional[set] = None,
    ) -> Any:
        """
        Default runner: one full agent turn (tools included) on the shift card.

        The import is local so the service can be imported without the AI stack.
        The event manager is built lazily: without it every turn failed before
        the first model call when the background worker ran the shift.
        """
        from codx.junior.chat.chat_engine import ChatEngine

        engine = ChatEngine(
            settings=self.settings,
            event_manager=self._event_manager(),
            user=self.user,
            tool_allowlist=tool_allowlist,
        )
        await engine.chat_with_project(chat=chat, system=system)
        return chat

    # -- shift card -------------------------------------------------------

    def _user_message(self, prompt: str) -> Any:
        """Build the user message that continues a shift."""
        from codx.junior.db import Message

        return Message(role="user", content=str(prompt or ""), user=self.user)

    def _create_shift_card(
        self,
        *,
        name: str,
        board: str,
        prompt: str,
        agenda: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        description: str = "",
        budget_cap: Optional[float] = None,
    ) -> Any:
        """Create the card of the shift on the desk board."""
        from codx.junior.task_manager import TaskManager

        names = ", ".join(item["name"] for item in agenda[:5]) or "free shift"
        task = TaskManager(settings=self.settings).create_task(
            name=f"Shift · {utcnow_iso()[:16].replace('T', ' ')}",
            description=(
                description
                or f"Autonomous shift of **{name}**. Agenda: {names}."
            ),
            content=prompt,
            board=board,
            column=C.SHIFT_COLUMN,
            status="doing",
            priority="high" if agenda else "medium",
            profiles=[name],
            tags=["actor", "shift"],
            # The chat budget is a hard stop inside the agent loop; the shift
            # loop also checks it between turns. Passing it here is what keeps a
            # single runaway turn from overspending the actor budget.
            estimation_cost=(
                float(budget_cap)
                if budget_cap is not None and float(budget_cap) > 0
                else None
            ),
        )
        try:
            task.meta_data = {**(getattr(task, "meta_data", None) or {}), "actor": {
                "actor": name,
                "board": board,
                "agenda": [item["id"] for item in agenda],
                "started_at": utcnow_iso(),
                "budget_cap": budget_cap,
            }}
            self._manager().save_chat(chat=task)
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - metadata is best effort
            logger.debug("actors: cannot stamp shift metadata: %s", ex)
        return task

    def _close_stale_shift_cards(
        self, actor: str, board: str, max_age_seconds: Optional[int] = None
    ) -> None:
        """
        Move abandoned shift cards out of ``Working`` before starting a new one.

        A crash or a failed first turn before this release could leave cards in
        ``Working`` forever. The actor lock guarantees no other shift of this
        actor is live here, and the timestamp threshold protects a card from a
        worker that is still finishing after a restart overlap. The threshold is
        at least the maximum runtime of a shift plus a grace period, so a long
        but healthy shift is never closed as stale.
        """
        if not board:
            return
        age = max(
            C.STALE_SHIFT_SECONDS,
            int(max_age_seconds or 0),
        )
        cutoff = utcnow() - timedelta(seconds=age)
        try:
            chats = self._manager().list_chats() or []
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - board cleanup is best effort
            logger.debug("actors: cannot scan stale shift cards: %s", ex)
            return
        for chat in chats:
            try:
                if str(getattr(chat, "board", "") or "") != board:
                    continue
                if str(getattr(chat, "column", "") or "") != C.SHIFT_COLUMN:
                    continue
                tags = {str(tag) for tag in (getattr(chat, "tags", []) or [])}
                if "shift" not in tags:
                    continue
                meta = getattr(chat, "meta_data", None) or {}
                actor_meta = meta.get("actor") if isinstance(meta, dict) else {}
                if isinstance(actor_meta, dict) and actor_meta.get("actor") not in ("", None, actor):
                    continue
                updated = parse_iso(
                    getattr(chat, "updated_at", "") or getattr(chat, "created_at", "")
                )
                if updated is None or updated > cutoff:
                    continue
                self._close_shift_card(
                    chat, error="Recovered an abandoned shift card from Working."
                )
                logger.info(
                    "actors: recovered stale shift card '%s' of '%s'",
                    getattr(chat, "id", ""),
                    actor,
                )
            except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - one bad card is not fatal
                logger.debug("actors: cannot recover stale shift card: %s", ex)

    def _close_shift_card(self, chat: Any, error: str = "") -> None:
        """
        Move the shift card out of ``Working`` so the board keeps a readable history.

        A failed first turn must still close its card: leaving it in ``Working``
        made the desk board look like the actor was permanently busy and hid the
        real error. The error is appended to the description so it survives even
        when no report was produced.
        """
        try:
            chat.status = "error" if error else "done"
            chat.column = C.SHIFT_DONE_COLUMN
            chat.progress = 0 if error else 100
            if error:
                note = f"\n\n**Shift failed:** {_clip(error, 2000)}"
                chat.description = f"{getattr(chat, 'description', '') or ''}{note}"[:8000]
            self._manager().save_chat(chat=chat)
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            logger.warning("actors: cannot close shift card: %s", ex)

    @staticmethod
    def _chat_cost(chat: Any) -> float:
        """Return the accumulated cost of a chat."""
        try:
            return float(getattr(chat, "cost", 0) or 0)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return 0.0

    def _read_turn(self, chat: Any) -> Tuple[str, float]:
        """Return the final answer and the cost accumulated by the chat."""
        content = ""
        for message in reversed(getattr(chat, "messages", []) or []):
            if str(getattr(message, "role", "")) == "assistant":
                content = str(getattr(message, "content", "") or "")
                break
        return content, self._chat_cost(chat)

    def _consume_agenda(self, agenda: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
        """
        Settle the ``wake_at`` of the delivered tasks without losing work.

        A task is consumed only when it is **closed**: the actor finished it.
        A task that is still open keeps its due wake and is delivered again on
        the next shift (the actor is expected to close it or schedule a new
        follow-up). A task the actor rescheduled to the future keeps that new
        wake. This replaces the old "always clear every agenda item" behavior,
        which silently dropped work whenever the shift failed, ran out of budget
        or was a dry run.
        """
        for item in agenda or []:
            chat_id = str(item.get("id") or item.get("chat_id") or "")
            if not chat_id:
                continue
            try:
                chat = self._manager().find_by_id(chat_id=chat_id)
            except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                logger.debug("actors: cannot read task '%s': %s", chat_id, ex)
                continue
            if chat is None:
                continue
            current = str(getattr(chat, "wake_at", "") or "")
            if not current or not is_due(current):
                # Already cleared by the actor, or rescheduled for later.
                continue
            if not self._is_closed(chat):
                # Still open: keep the wake so the next shift can finish it.
                continue
            schedule = str(getattr(chat, "schedule", "") or "").strip()
            if schedule:
                # Recurring task: the run happened, arm the next occurrence
                # instead of consuming the alarm clock.
                self._rearm(chat, schedule)
                continue
            try:
                chat.wake_at = ""
                self._manager().save_chat(chat=chat)
                logger.info("actors: consumed wake of closed task '%s'", chat_id)
            except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                logger.warning("actors: cannot consume wake of '%s': %s", chat_id, ex)

    # -- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def _started(state: ActorState, name: str, board: str) -> ActorState:
        """Mark the state as running (called under the state lock)."""
        state.mark_started(name, board)
        return state

    @staticmethod
    def _instructions(profile: Any, config: ActorConfig) -> str:
        """Compose the mandate of the actor: profile content + standing orders."""
        parts = [
            str(getattr(profile, "content", "") or "").strip(),
            str(config.instructions or "").strip(),
        ]
        return "\n\n---\n\n".join([part for part in parts if part])

    @staticmethod
    def _summary_from(content: str) -> str:
        """Extract the shift summary from the report."""
        text = str(content or "").strip()
        if not text:
            return ""
        marker = "## Shift report"
        index = text.find(marker)
        return text[index:] if index >= 0 else text

    def _emit(self, actor: str, event: str, message: str = "", **data: Any) -> None:
        """Notify connected clients (best effort)."""
        manager = self._event_manager()
        if manager is None:
            return
        emit = getattr(manager, "autonomy_event", None)
        if not callable(emit):
            return
        try:
            emit({
                "actor": actor,
                "agent": actor,
```

```py api/codx/junior/autonomy/service.py
"""
Application service of the actors.

One **shift** of one actor is a bounded pipeline:

    actor configuration -> boards -> agenda (due tasks)
        -> shift card on the desk board -> one or more agent turns with the
        whole tool set -> report on the card -> state store

This module is the **single runtime**. It used to be two:

* ``autonomy`` — a profile woke up, read its board and worked with every tool;
* ``board_manager`` — a profile reviewed a board and answered with a JSON
  action contract that was validated and applied afterwards.

The only real differences were the prompt (role), the tool policy and whether a
shift is one turn or turns until the work is done. Those are now three fields of
:class:`~codx.junior.autonomy.models.ActorConfig` (``role``, ``policy``,
``session``), and both entry points share this pipeline. The JSON contract is
gone: an actor uses the same task tools a human uses, so every change it makes
is visible on the board exactly like a human change.

Two things make this different from a chat:

* the actor is woken by the scheduler, not by a user, and it must decide by
  itself what to do (see :mod:`.prompts`);
* every follow-up becomes a **scheduled task** (``wake_at``), which is what makes
  "check that system again in two days" possible without a human in the loop.

The **weekly schedule** is enforced here as well: an actor only starts a shift
inside its availability window, and a due task that falls outside the window is
kept (its ``wake_at`` is not consumed) until the next opening.

Everything heavy (the AI stack, the chat engine) is imported lazily and both the
turn runner and the chat factory are injectable, so the whole pipeline can be
tested offline and the module can be imported by the API without the AI deps.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
```
